styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's numbers look good: 24 visible tones per tile (references 9-20), 0% near-flat coverage, and no 5x5 flat fills. But 80% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, while the same-kind references with real bodies are tinted (stall-cheese 1%, hedge 0%, well-roofed 33%). That matches the picture: a uniform dark outline around the whole counter and toys, which reads as the 'sticker' look rather than dark-material-tone edges. The main counter body has a shallow ramp, with about 3 steps on the purple/pink front and the glass band. It is mostly flat bands with small dots of toys and prizes. The tone count is inflated by the small colourful toys and trinkets, not by shaded material ramps like the stall's cloth, wood and awning. Next to the stall and well it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails on outline and shading depth.

styleAnswer.evidence: On the measured facts the candidate matches or beats the references on density: 24 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, with 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. Its main weakness is the outline. 80% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% on the hedge and stall and 33% on the well. The dark line around the counter body and glass case reads as a uniform near-black contour, not the dark tone of the adjacent material, which is the 'sticker' look. The purple front panel and trim carry only about 3-4 lightness steps, and the prize case and plush toys are small clusters with little internal shading. The references show 5-6 steps with tinted edges. Density is good, but the neutral outline and the shallower ramps keep it below the Beodeul bar, so it fails.
